messages:
maria: Quick sync — proposing a hybrid capacity-aware / price-quantile bid strategy for spot GPU pools. Goal: keep 95th-percentile latency SLO while shaving avg cost by ~20%. Thoughts?

aj: +1 on hybrid. My take: use capacity signals as a hard constraint (don't bid below capacity_score threshold) and use price quantiles to set bids per-region. Example config idea: 
```
{\n  "bid_strategy": "capacity_first_then_price_quantile",\n  "capacity_threshold": 0.7,\n  "price_quantile": 0.25,\n  "warm_pool_pct": 0.12\n}
```
Short rationale: reserve a small warm buffer in each ASG, then let price quantile dial aggressiveness.

sudip: Need to think about interruptions — if we keep only 12% warm pool we still see preempts during spikes. What's the plan for quick spill-to-dedicated? Any fallback ordering?

maria: fallback order: 1) local warm buffer, 2) cross-region sibling pool, 3) dedicated reserve (burstable), 4) degrade to smaller model on same hardware. We should encode policy with timeouts: warm buffer TTL 90s, cross-region failover 2m, dedicated fallback immediate if SLO-critical.

lee: Where do we get capacity_score? From spot-availability telemetry + recent reclaim rates? I've been experimenting with 5m windows combining free capacity and recent spot loss probability. Score formula: (1 - recent_reclaim_rate) * normalized_free_capacity. Works pretty well in us-west-2 and eu-central.

aj: Nice. Also add a jittered bidding timer so we don't flood the market simultaneously on big reclaim events — random backoff 0-30s per instance group.

ops-bot: [alert] capacity_signal: us-west-2-gpu: capacity_score dropped from 0.82 -> 0.56 in last 3m (spike). Recommend promoting warm buffer and switching price_quantile -> 0.1 for region.

maria: ops-bot noted. I'll push a canary change: reduce quantile to 0.1 and increase warm_pool_pct to 18% for us-west-2. Patching policy now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: ref infra/spot-bid/quantile-hybrid v2.3 -> prod (maria). Commit: 9a1b7c.

sudip: Quick note on stateful workers: we need safe draining hooks for CUDA worker persistence — ensure KV cache checkpoint before preempt handling, 30s grace for checkpoints. If no checkpoint, fallback to immediate eviction and restart on dedicated.

lee: Also recommend a rolling experiment: route 10% of traffic through price-optimized-only pools for 48h to measure tail latencies and actual cost delta. Might find cheaper spots without hurting SLOs.

maria: Agreed. Plan: canary 10% price-only in ap-southeast-1 and ca-central for 48h, measure p50/p95/p99 latency and cost/unit. If p99 rises > 10% abort.

aj: Can we add an eval hook to inject targeted prompts that exercise long context runs to surface KV-cache misses during the canary? Small script: `./scripts/loadtest-ctx.sh --seq 2048 --rps 5`

maria: Good idea. Add that to canary runbook. I'll update the runbook and alert thresholds.

sudip: One more: make rack-aware allocations aware of GPU memory fragmentation. Some instances show lower usable memory after long runs — add a mem-frag metric and prefer lower-frag hosts when making warm buffer assignments.

lee: I'll add mem_frag to the prioritization vector. We should also tag instances with `warm_candidate:true` after a successful health-check pass.

maria: Thanks all. I'll post the updated config + runbook in #eng-infra once deploy completes. :thumbsup:
